text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- In a suprise turn of events, the government postpones debate on a motion in which the ruling Kenya African National Union (Kanu) seeks to wrest control of the Public Accounts and Public Investment committees from the opposition.
- Both factions of opposition party FORD-Kenya, say they are ready to meet to resolve their leadership crisis.

- Local relief agencies say the Kenya government and non-governmental organisations should start preparing for an emergency situation in the drought-stricken areas of Eastern and North-Eastern provinces.
- Three men suspected of killing two policemen at Sagana town in the key coffee and tea growing Central Kenya, apparently paid unsuspecting villagers to help them escape.
- The Government releases cheques amounting to six million shillings to be distributed to relatives of the 1994 Mtongwe ferry disaster.
- A Member of Parliament Matu Wamae, says the government has borrowed 81 billion shillings from local banks forcing them to increase their interest rates by 20 percent.
- Ten Kenyans-- five women and five children -- are gunned down by people suspected of having crossed into the country from neighbouring Ethiopia.
